subject: Segmentation evidence & diagram handoff for Redwood private VPC
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyrcloud.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Segmentation evidence + diagram request for Redwood private VPC

Markus / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SOC readiness checklist I promised to share the segmentation evidence from our side and ask you to validate the control/data separation before we sign off on the on-prem deployment. Attached is a short packet with packet-capture snapshots and VLAN mappings (zephyr-seg-proof.pdf).

High-level asks from our audit team:
- Confirm the control-plane mgmt networks are logically isolated from tenant data paths (including KV cache traffic).
- Point us to the diagram you want us to reference in the final evidence folder.
- Confirm expected egress-control points where we should collect flow logs for retention.

Can you confirm the list and tell us which artifacts you need from Zephyr for the handoff? We aim to close this loop by end of week.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | ZephyrCloud
[Attachment: zephyr-seg-proof.pdf (pdf)]
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyrcloud.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation evidence + diagram request for Redwood private VPC

Alex — thanks for the packet. We reviewed the PDF and have a few clarifying requests before we provide a formal validation.

Quick answers up front:
- We will validate control-plane isolation (management plane / orchestration controllers) against your captures and return a signed checklist.
- For diagrams, please reference our canonical runbook diagram (see link in later notes) — we will attach a tailored diagram for Zephyr once we confirm address pools.
- Egress collection points: we expect flow logs at the tenant-edge router and the egress-proxy cluster (both must be exported to your SIEM).

To proceed we need:
1) Exact CIDR ranges used for Zephyr tenant data lanes (both east-west and north-south).
2) The PoP-level VLAN IDs used in your switch fabric for the tenant (so we can stamp the diagram).
3) Any additional mTLS trust domains used by your observability agents (we need them listed for cert rotation notes).

I've attached our internal checklist for segmentation proofing (redwood-vpc-seg-checklist.xlsx) — fill the top section and return. Priyom and Naomi are on the thread for architecture sign-off.

Next step: if you can fill the checklist and send back the VLAN/CIDR table, we'll aim to produce the stamped diagram and the formal evidence email.

Best,
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-vpc-seg-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyrcloud.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation evidence + diagram request for Redwood private VPC

Alex — quick technical notes from the architecture review (inline):

> Confirm the control-plane mgmt networks are logically isolated from tenant data paths (including KV cache traffic).
>
> (Alex) see packet captures attached.

We inspected the packet captures in zephyr-seg-proof.pdf. Observations:
- The controller API plane is on a separate /24 from tenant data; control-plane traffic terminates on management-only NICs bound to the orchestration fabric.
- We observed an anomalous ARP entry in capture #3 — please confirm whether that is a transient management probe or an incorrectly-staged interface.
- KV cache traffic should always be sourced from the runtime host loopback to avoid accidental export to the tenant VLANs. Ensure the host-level iptables rule is present (I can share the snippet).

Attached an egress flow diagram that mirrors our expected layout (egress-flow.svg). Key items to validate on your side:
- Tenant egress must pass through the egress-proxy cluster (port 3128) before reaching external networks.
- Flow logs must be exported in tranche windows of 6 hours for compliance retention.

If you can confirm the ARP anomaly and provide the CIDR/VLAN table Markus requested, I can sign off on the control/data separation and generate the stamped diagram.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Staff Network Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: egress-flow.svg (svg)]
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyrcloud.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 14:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation evidence + diagram request for Redwood private VPC

Naomi / Markus,

Thanks — we dug into the ARP entry. That was a transient probe from a fabric switch during a firmware upgrade window; confirmed not from any tenant host. I've attached an expanded evidence pack with a short change-log (zephyr-seg-review.pdf) and the filled checklist section. VLAN/CIDR table is below:

- Tenant data east-west: 10.200.0.0/16
- Tenant data north-south (ingress): 10.210.0.0/20
- Management/control plane: 172.31.50.0/24
- VLANs: 110 (tenant-data), 120 (tenant-ingress), 200 (mgmt)
- Observability agents: trust-domain=zeph-obsv; cert-renewal=90d

We also uploaded the full pcap and a signed statement to the handoff folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-zephyr-handbook

Next: can you provide the stamped diagram and a short paragraph we can include in our audit evidence that says Redwood validated control/data separation and the egress collection points?

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | ZephyrCloud
[Attachment: zephyr-seg-review.pdf (pdf)]
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zephyrcloud.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation evidence & diagram handoff for Redwood private VPC

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and the VLAN/CIDR table. We've reviewed the additional artifacts and Naomi's notes.

Acceptance notes (for your audit folder):
- Redwood confirms logical separation between control-plane (172.31.50.0/24) and tenant data (10.200.0.0/16, 10.210.0.0/20).
- Egress collection points validated at tenant-edge router and egress-proxy cluster. We recommend exporting NetFlow to your SIEM at both points (sample config in link).
- Observability agent trust-domain and cert rotation cadence accepted.

Attached: stamped diagram (we've put a copy in the shared runbook folder) and a one-paragraph statement you can paste into your audit evidence. Final operational step: confirm a date for scheduling the cutover smoke test — we suggest week of Jan 11, 2027.

Link to runbook artifact: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_redwood_runbook
Jira with follow-up tasks: INF-2247

Next steps: Alex to confirm cutover window and Zephyr to enable flow export to SIEM.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Manager, On-Prem Deployments | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-stamped-diagram.svg (svg)]
